The JET Li-BES system consists of 26 spatial channels along the neutral lithium beam.
The 26 lines of sight are not perpendicular to the beam direction, causing Doppler shifts of the lithium beam emission.
The instrumental function and interference filter curve are modeled using Gaussian processes with hyperparameters determined by maximizing the evidence.
The Poisson noise from photon statistics and electronic noise are included in the likelihood function.
The prior distributions for the lithium line intensity, Bremsstrahlung background, and instrumental offset are chosen as Gaussians with large standard deviations.
The posterior distributions are obtained using Bayesian linear Gaussian inversion.
The estimated spectra agree well with the measured spectra for the analyzed channels.
For channel 16, an extra peak in the measured spectrum is observed due to impurity line radiation, which is not captured by the model.
The intensity profile of the lithium line radiation is subsequently used to reconstruct the edge electron density profile.
The Bayesian approach allows the separation of signal and background without the need for beam modulation.
The method can be applied generally to improve spectral fitting for other systems.
The work was supported by the National Research Foundation of Korea and the EUROfusion Consortium.
The authors include researchers from KAIST, Max-Planck-Institut für Plasmaphysik, and Culham Science Centre.
The paper was published in the Journal of Applied Physics in 2018.
The JET Li-BES system is widely used to measure edge electron density profiles in fusion research.
